body:
I can confirm this for v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f]

My thoughts on this are:
 - The way the colors render works as intended. What happens with the transparency is that Godots internal tools for drawing Navigation Shapes takes in the debug color and multiplies it with multiple other color constants depending on stuff like where the debug color is used (edge, face, selected, not selected, etc.), meaning yes, there is an effective maximum transparency (at least when setting the color though the color picker, as that doesn't allow for >1.0 values). On play though with "Navigation visible" this gets skipped due to some of these distinctions not making sense in that context, so the originally set (unmodified full opacity) color is granted.
- The way faces are "off" in color is intentional too, as can bee seen in solid.colors.mp4, the colors get slightly hue shifted for each face to make it easier to distinguish them. Similar can be seen when showing the debug shape for the CollisionPolygon2D, although I think the solution here is even more elegant than that, because randomly hue-shifting is way more true to the ProjectSettings than just continuously advancing the hue with an irrational fraction as seen in `CollisionPolygon2D`.

- The only thing that should work but doesn't in my mind is the **edge color not refreshed correctly when `debug/shapes/navigation/3d/geometry_edge_color` is changed**. (it works perfectly for the faces as we can see)
I assume this bug has something to do with how the edges change appearance with the `NavigationRegion3D` being enabled or not, but this is just a wild guess must be confirmed in code. The way the edge color is "correct" in game is consistent with it refreshing after restarting the editor. And the fact that restarting the scene, doing things all over again in a new one, or baking a new navmesh doesn't work, points towards the color not being refreshed in some singleton that only gets refreshed when the program restarts.

I would like to look further into this is no one else just had an epiphany and knows exactly where too look from this...

> * The way faces are "off" in color is intentional too, as can bee seen in solid.colors.mp4, the colors get slightly hue shifted for each face to make it easier to distinguish them. 

The "off" I meant was mainly the fact it seems the color chosen is not correct, with very small changes in color.
It feels like no matter what color hues I choose there, there is only a small difference in color in mostly the same tones.
So something is off about how it is setting/mixing the colors.

> * The only thing that should work but doesn't in my mind is the **edge color not refreshed correctly when `debug/shapes/navigation/3d/geometry_edge_color` is changed**. (it works perfectly for the faces as we can see)

You are completely right there. I think this is a real bug. The Edge Color doesn't update at all until a project reload.
I only saw that the colors worked properly after restarting the editor after saving the MRP.
Your logic for the problem is most likely correct too.

---

It seems the transparency color is kinda working now?
Maybe it fixed itself on the project restart, or I didn't had it selected when testing. (But I could have swear I had it)

But the real issue with the **inconsistent colors still exists**.
It changes to a brown-ish when changing it inside the editor(maybe mixing the color instead of setting it).
And when restarting the editor it gets the correct color. Turning it white.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ce200b2-fa4c-4acd-9446-51828c9f7b5b

It seems changing the debug face color is mixing it with the color that it started when the project was first loaded, instead of setting or adjusting the color. So something is wrong there.

---

Turns out the NavigationRegion3D code never uses the DebugColor properly.
It loads it correctly when first creating the material.

But **on the redraw**, it applies it as a **vertex color on top of the created material**.
And it only does that when random colors is enabled. If you disable random colors it doesn't do anything to change colors.

Here is the redraw sections if you want to take a look

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/95baa6f29a89416ecd0afa546e62032479739891/modules/navigation_3d/editor/navigation_region_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp#L165-L184

**It is missing updating the albedo for all the 4 materials inside the redraw function.**
RIght now it only sets it inside the constructor when the materials are first created. Hence why it works after re-starting the project.

The gizmos have their own material logic to work with gizmo options. They dont use the exact same properties as the rest of the debug as they run into a lot of z-fighting and transparency issues with their own stuff.

The gizmo materials are created at plugin creation, aka editor start. So they only read the debug values from the NavigationServer once.
The actual debug outside gizmo is all rendered by the nodes using the colors and materials stored and shared from the NavigationServer.

The node blocks its own debug rendering inside the editor, else it would render the correct debug and the gizmo debug on top.
Gizmos are the weird one here. They require visuals internally to not be culled by the editor clickable BVH tree. So you cant just have the gizmo with collision only and let the node render its proper debug, no you need to disable the proper debug and let the weird gizmo debug render.

What could be done is connect the gizmos to the xyz_debug_changed signals of the server or the projectsettings directly. It might still not look fully the same because the materials are not guaranteed to be placed the same (e.g. have same transparency index).
